transcript.text: Hi, my Hotpoint Aquarius dryer is taking forever to dry and the top gets really hot. Model is TCM580GUK if that helps

The symptoms you describe, long drying times and a hot top, almost always mean restricted airflow, usually from lint build-up. On a condenser dryer like the TCM580G, this is also a fire risk, so it's worth sorting out before using it again.

## ⚠️ First: Check the safety recall
Many Hotpoint condenser dryers made between roughly 2004 and 2015, including TCM580 models, were part of Whirlpool's fire safety modification programme because lint could contact the heating element. Before anything else:
• Find the model and serial number on the sticker inside the door rim.
• Enter it into the tumble dryer safety checker on the Hotpoint UK website, or call Hotpoint customer services.
• If it's affected and hasn't been modified, stop using it. The fix is free.

## Things to check and clean
Unplug the dryer first.

1. Door lint filter
• Pull out the filter in the door opening and clean it after every load.
• If it looks clogged or greasy (fabric softener residue), wash it in warm soapy water and let it dry fully.

2. Condenser unit (most likely culprit)
• Open the flap/kickplate at the bottom front.
• Unclip the condenser (the rectangular block) and slide it out.
• Rinse it under a shower or outside with a hose, through the fins in both directions, until water runs clear. They often get packed with fluff.
• Let it drain, and check the rubber seals are intact before refitting.
• Do this roughly every month.

3. Condenser housing
• With the condenser out, use a torch to look inside the cavity. Vacuum or wipe out any fluff.

4. Water container
• Empty it after each load. A full container stops the cycle or affects performance.

5. Usage factors
• Don't overload. Half to two-thirds full lets air circulate.
• Spin clothes at a high speed in the washer first.
• Make sure the room isn't too warm or enclosed. Condenser dryers need cool air around them.
• Leave a gap at the back and sides for ventilation.

## If it's still slow or overheating
If cleaning doesn't help, possible faults include a failing thermostat, a worn fan, or a blocked internal duct. These need an engineer. Given the dryer's age and the fire risk, it may also be worth weighing repair against replacement.

Thank you. I had a look: the door filter had a thick layer of fluff on it (I'll admit I sometimes forget to clean it), and the condenser had lint packed on the fins. I rinsed the condenser and it looks much cleaner now. I can't see any green 'safety modified' sticker, and I don't know if it was ever modified. I also often run the dryer while I'm out at work, so should I stop doing that?

Well done for getting stuck in. A heavily clogged filter and packed condenser fins very likely explain both the slow drying and the hot top. But there are two important safety points.

## 1. Check the recall before using it again
The missing sticker doesn't tell you much either way. Stickers can fall off or be missed, and some machines were never modified. The only reliable check is the serial number:

• Find the model and serial number on the label inside the door rim.
• Enter them into the tumble dryer safety checker on the Hotpoint UK website, or call Hotpoint's recall line (number on their site).
• If it's affected and unmodified, don't use it at all until it's been fixed or replaced. This is free.
• If it comes back as not affected or already modified, you're fine to carry on.

The clogged lint is exactly what made the affected models dangerous, so this check really matters in your case.

## 2. Yes, stop running it while you're out
UK fire services and manufacturers advise never leaving a tumble dryer running unattended, including when you're out or asleep. Dryers are a common cause of house fires, and a fire that starts while you're home can usually be caught early. One that starts while you're at work can take hold of the whole house.

Safer habits:
• Run it when you're home and awake, and let it finish its cool-down phase before you leave.
• Clean the door filter after every load. A quick routine helps, like clearing it while the clothes are still warm.
• Rinse the condenser about once a month.
• Empty the water container each time.
• Keep the area around the dryer clear and make sure you have a working smoke alarm nearby.

## If it's still slow after cleaning
If it's confirmed safe and still takes too long or the top stays very hot, the fault may be internal: a blocked internal duct, a failing fan, thermostat, heating element or humidity sensor. That's a job for a qualified engineer rather than DIY, since it involves mains wiring and the heating parts.
